## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

The historical statement excluding modeling error is too broad. Define the full and individual finite perturbations relative to the same baseline, with compatible inputs and initial states. Under those definitions a within-model interaction residual can expose nonlinear coupling. In a model-to-data comparison it can additionally contain parameter, sensor and numerical errors.

Exact first variations around the same nominal motion superpose without such a residual. Bounds for finite perturbations require smoothness, a declared scaled norm and controlled propagation. Coordinate Hessians must not be called intrinsic curvature without a specified geometric construction. See [canonical residuals](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-4-residuals-curvature.html).

Current reading path: [Canonical Series Article](/articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-4-residuals-curvature.html).

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Historical Draft: Superseded Wording"}

## Interaction Residuals

Residuals arise from curvature, not modeling error.

$$
\Delta x_{res} = \Delta x_{full} - \sum_i \Delta x_i
$$

## Interpretation

Residuals quantify higher-order coupling terms.

:::
